title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## LLM‑Controlled Robot Arm Paint Showdown

### The Breakthrough
The demo hooked Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT‑6 Astra into a robot arm’s control loop, letting each LLM generate motion primitives that drove brush strokes on a canvas. Both models operated on the same hardware, producing paintings in real time, demonstrating an end‑to‑end LLM‑to‑actuation pipeline for manipulation.

### The Caveats
The comparison rests on a single anecdotal demo with no repeat trials, quantitative metrics, or baseline comparisons.

## Unitree G1+ Humanoid Upgrade

### The Breakthrough
Unitree released the G1+ humanoid, adding two neck DoFs, boosting peak shoulder‑and‑waist torque by 110% and arm torque by 43%, plus a binocular wide‑angle vision system, head‑touch sensors, a six‑mic array and external power support. These upgrades aim to improve agility, perception and human‑robot interaction on the same price‑point platform.

### The Caveats
The performance gains are unverified, as the announcement provides no quantitative data or direct comparison to the original G1.

## 2026 Inference Hardware Revolution

### The Breakthrough
The article highlights three 2026 inference hardware advances: Cerebras’s wafer‑scale engine that colocates memory and compute to eliminate KV‑cache bandwidth bottlenecks; Nvidia’s Groq 3 LPU that orders on‑chip SRAM and compute blocks to cut data movement; and Amazon’s split‑inference pipeline that offloads KV‑cache handling to Cerebras while running model layers on Trainium. Together they shift industry focus from training‑centric to inference‑centric AI compute.

### The Caveats
The piece offers no benchmarks or real‑world measurements, relying solely on vendor statements.

## Foxglove SDK for Multimodal Logging

### The Breakthrough
Foxglove SDK provides a unified Rust API for writing sensor data to MCAP files and streaming it live over WebSocket, with pre‑built binaries and wheels that let Python and C++ users avoid compiling Rust. Built‑in ROS/ROS2 integration and schema support enable seamless multimodal logging for robotic experiments.

### The Caveats
The SDK ships without empirical evaluation or comparison to existing logging tools, so its claimed advantages are unverified.

## Franken Surveillance System Design

### The Breakthrough
The Franken surveillance system design introduces four operational planes and an immutable EvidenceDeltaBatch stream, using semantic MVCC and ATP object graphs to guarantee provenance‑rich world models, plus a Rust‑only cognitive OS that consumes SituationCapsules and a digital‑twin calibration workflow using piloted drones.

### The Caveats
The repository only contains design specifications; there is no working implementation of video capture, model inference, or alerting, so the claimed capabilities have not been demonstrated.

### Priority
Seeing two state‑of‑the‑art LLMs directly control a robot arm provides a concrete glimpse of how large language models are moving from text to physical manipulation, making it the most immediate and eye‑catching development for robotics readers today.

### One action
If you have access to a low‑cost 6‑DoF arm, try hooking an open‑source LLM via a simple motion‑primitive API (e.g., using the Foxglove SDK for data logging) to experiment with end‑to‑end control.

### What to watch
Both the LLM‑driven painting demo and Unitree’s G1+ upgrade showcase hardware‑level progress, but they target different trajectories—software‑centric manipulation versus platform‑centric actuation and sensing. Tracking follow‑up demos that quantify performance for the LLM pipeline and real‑world benchmarks for the G1+ will reveal which approach drives faster advances in embodied AI.
